title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor
hook: Chopin’s first concerto, with a slow movement inspired by a young singer he loved in silence.

painting.title: View of the Kazimierz Palace from Powiśle
painting.pairingNote: The Warsaw University palace above the Vistula, where Chopin went to school and beside which he grew up; painted in the decade after he wrote this concerto and left the city for good.

facts: Chopin wrote this concerto in Warsaw between the autumn of 1829 and the early spring of 1830, when he had just finished his studies. He was nineteen. It was the first of his two piano concertos; it is called No. 2 only because it was published second.

After two run-throughs at home and among friends, he played it in public on 17 March 1830 at the National Theatre in Warsaw. It was his first big concert in his own city. Seven months later he left Poland, and he never returned.

In a letter of 3 October 1829 to his friend Tytus Woyciechowski he wrote of his “ideal”, whom he had loved in silence for six months, and who “inspired the Adagio of my Concerto”. His biographers agree that she was the young singer Konstancja Gładkowska. The published concerto, however, is dedicated to Countess Delfina Potocka.

As in his other concerto, the orchestra frames the piano rather than competing with it. The piano sings like an opera singer, in long, ornamented melodies, and the dances of Poland are never far away: a mazurka rhythm in the first movement, a kujawiak in the last.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a proud, sorrowful Allegro in a mazurka’s rhythm (I), a nocturne for a secret love (II), a Polish country dance that ends in F major (III).

movements.heading: Maestoso
movements.summary: The orchestra first presents the two main themes on its own: a proud, sorrowful tune in a dotted rhythm, and a gentle song in a major key. Then the piano enters with a dramatic flourish and makes both themes its own, decorated with runs and trills. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]].

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a solemn, dotted tune in F minor, with the lilt of a slow mazurka.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a tender, singing melody in A-flat major, like a nocturne.

stops.hear: Quiet strings play a solemn tune in a dotted rhythm; soon the whole orchestra takes it up loudly
stops.happening: Theme 1, in F minor, in the orchestral introduction

stops.hear: The music softens; the woodwinds sing a gentle tune in a major key
stops.happening: Theme 2, first heard in the orchestra

stops.hear: The piano enters alone with a forceful, sweeping flourish, then plays the solemn first tune, richly decorated
stops.happening: The piano’s entry and its version of Theme 1

stops.hear: The piano sings a tender melody in A-flat major, over soft strings
Brilliant runs and leaps in the piano, faster and faster
The orchestra alone, loud
Quiet and searching, then a torrent of rapid piano figures, rising to a loud climax in the full orchestra
The two themes return, woven together

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The piano races through a last brilliant passage; the orchestra closes the movement in F minor

notice: Listen to how long the orchestra plays before the piano enters, over three minutes here. When the piano comes in, notice how it takes the same tunes and turns them into something more personal and decorated.
Follow the dotted rhythm of the first theme. It keeps returning, in the orchestra and the piano, through the whole movement.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Zimerman recorded both concertos in 1999 with the Polish Festival Orchestra, which he formed for the 150th anniversary of Chopin’s death and directed from the piano. His tempos are unusually broad: the slow movement lasts over eleven minutes, where many pianists take about nine. On the Spotify album the concerto is tracks 4–6, after the First Concerto.

movements.heading: Larghetto
movements.summary: A [[nocturne|nocturne]] for piano and orchestra, and the movement Chopin wrote for his “ideal”. The piano sings a long, slow melody, and each time it returns it is more richly decorated, like an opera singer ornamenting an aria. In the middle the mood breaks: over trembling strings, the piano declaims a dramatic, speech-like passage in octaves.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a long, slow, singing melody in A-flat major, decorated with trills and runs.

mainIdeas.name: The outburst
mainIdeas.description: a passionate passage in the minor, the piano in bare octaves over a string [[tremolo|tremolo]], like an operatic [[recitative|recitative]].

stops.hear: A few bars of soft, warm strings
The piano sings a slow, tender melody, decorated with little turns and trills
stops.happening: The main theme, in A-flat major

stops.hear: The melody returns, even more decorated, with long, delicate runs
The mood darkens; the strings tremble, and the piano declaims in bare, loud octaves, as if speaking
stops.happening: The middle section, in A-flat minor: a [[recitative|recitative]] over [[tremolo|tremolo]]

stops.hear: Calm returns; the piano sings the melody once more, with its richest decoration
A bassoon joins the piano with its own soft line

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The piano’s last ornaments; the movement fades in A-flat major

notice: Compare the melody each time it returns. The tune stays the same; the decoration around it grows more elaborate.
In the middle section, listen for the change in the piano’s voice: from singing to speaking, in hard, bare octaves.

movements.heading: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A finale in the rhythm of the [[kujawiak|kujawiak]], a Polish country dance in three. Its main tune keeps coming back like a refrain, as in a [[rondo|rondo]]. In one episode the string players strike the strings with the wood of their bows, and near the end a horn call turns the music from F minor to a bright F major.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a graceful, lilting dance tune in F minor, first in the piano.

mainIdeas.name: The rustic episode
mainIdeas.description: a robust village tune in the piano, over string players tapping with the wood of the bow.

mainIdeas.name: The horn call
mainIdeas.description: a short signal that opens the F major ending.

stops.hear: The piano plays a graceful, lilting tune in three over a light accompaniment
stops.happening: The refrain, in F minor, marked *semplice ma graziosamente*

stops.hear: The orchestra takes up the dance, louder
Energetic, swaggering music with brilliant piano runs
The graceful tune returns
A sturdy country tune in the piano; underneath, the strings make dry, clicking sounds
stops.happening: The second episode, with [[col-legno|col legno]] strings. Chopin marks it *scherzando*

stops.hear: The refrain returns, then more brilliant episodes
A horn plays a short call

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: The music turns to F major; the piano races in glittering runs to a bright close

notice: In the second episode, listen for the clicking sound under the piano tune. It is the string players tapping with the wood of their bows, an unusual effect at the time.
Listen for the moment the horn sounds its call. Within seconds, the minor key of the whole concerto gives way to F major.

threads.title: The singer
threads.body: Chopin heard melody as a singer would, and his piano phrases breathe like long, ornamented arias, nowhere more than in the Larghetto.

threads.title: Poland
threads.body: The mazurka rhythm of the first movement and the kujawiak of the finale bring the dances of his homeland into the concert hall.

threads.title: Minor to major
threads.body: The concerto stays in the minor until its last minute and a half, and then turns to F major.
